question.text: Two vehicles, A and B, begin traveling at the same moment along a straight horizontal path in the identical forward direction. At time t = 0, vehicle A is located 10 m behind vehicle B. Vehicle A accelerates from rest at a uniform rate of a = 4 m/s², whereas vehicle B proceeds at a steady speed of v = 1 m/s. Calculate the time elapsed before vehicle A catches up to vehicle B.
conditions: motion along a straight line in the same direction
vehicles begin motion simultaneously at t = 0
initial separation is 10 m with car A behind car B
car A starts from rest with uniform acceleration a = 4 m/s²
car B travels with constant velocity v = 1 m/s

solution.approach: Write the position of each car as a function of time from a common origin and solve for the time at which the two positions become equal.

steps.text: Place car A at the origin at t = 0, with car B 10 m ahead of it. Car A starts from rest with constant acceleration; car B moves at constant velocity.
Car A overtakes car B when their positions are equal.
Solve the quadratic equation for t.
Keep only the positive root, since time cannot be negative.

common_mistakes.text: Keeping the negative root t = −2 s instead of discarding it can lead to picking the wrong sign in the final answer.
Writing car A's position as 4t² instead of 2t² by forgetting the half in ½at² gives a wrong quadratic and a wrong time.
